_comment: ISO/RTO interconnection-queue context for the grid-availability layer. queue_gw = approx generation capacity in the interconnection queue (GW, illustrative, LBNL 'Queued Up' order of magnitude); avg_wait_years = typical interconnection timeline; availability = 0-5 how easy it currently is to get large new load/generation connected (higher = more available / faster). Best-effort estimates for visualization, not authoritative.

PJM.name: PJM Interconnection
PJM.note: Largest queue; Northern Virginia transmission-constrained; multi-year waits and rising capacity prices.

MISO.name: MISO
MISO.note: Large queue but Midwest land/transmission relatively available; queue reform underway.

SPP.name: Southwest Power Pool
SPP.note: Wind-rich plains, space and headroom; generally faster than PJM/CAISO.

ERCOT.name: ERCOT (Texas)
ERCOT.note: Connect-and-manage: fastest large-load interconnection; energy-only market, weather/scarcity risk.

WECC.name: WECC (non-ISO West)
WECC.note: Utility-by-utility (APS, SRP, NV Energy, PacifiCorp); varies; often water-constrained.

CAISO.name: CAISO (California)
CAISO.note: Very large queue, expensive power, long interconnection timelines.

NYISO.name: NYISO (New York)
NYISO.note: Downstate constrained; cheaper, more available upstate (hydro).

SERC.name: Southeast (vertically integrated)
SERC.note: Duke/Southern/Dominion-South: bilateral utility deals, moderate availability and active DC recruitment.

TVA.name: Tennessee Valley Authority
TVA.note: Federal utility, proactive data-center recruitment; relatively available, low rates.
